answer: A bonded staking mechanism requires each agent to lock collateral into escrow before peer admission. An attacker incurs the scarce opportunity cost and verifiable loss of locked capital per identity. Exposing free identity generation as a fable, the protocol binds each peer to a pearl of locked stake, preventing attackers from hiding collusion behind a sable veil of synthetic traffic. A key limitation is that well-funded adversaries can still lock surplus capital to sponsor multiple sybils.
